text: 23-year-old female. The patient has been brought in by her boyfriend due to a 4-month history of feeling persistently sad. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizophrenia (with depressive features).

The clinical picture of a 23-year-old female presenting with a 7-month history of auditory hallucinations and a 4-month history of major depressive symptoms (sadness, sleep/appetite disturbance, poor concentration) is highly suggestive of schizophrenia with mood syndrome. The onset of psychosis (hallucinations) preceding the full depressive episode further supports this diagnosis over primary mood disorders. No further tests are required at this stage.
